audit.why: EVEN at 6/10 fits 46.49% over 114 games — the largest sample in this slice — and the phase shape (even to 5, Sylas at 6 and first item) matches a champion whose power is an ultimate steal and a scaling heal.
audit.corrected: Kept; the mechanics underneath are what changed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 section warns that Hijack steals your ultimate but gives no cooldowns, so the reader cannot see how lopsided the exchange is.
audit.why: Hijack is 80/55/30s. Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140s. At rank 1 he can steal roughly every second time yours is up; by rank 3 he has one nearly every fight while you have one every two and a half minutes. That single ratio is why 'never spend R in his sight' is a rule rather than a preference, and it was missing.
audit.corrected: 80s at rank 1 down to 30, against your 180 — the ult trade is never in your favour.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says Sylas's E is 'a dash plus a return chain-pull stun' and that he will 'land his E chain-pull stun to lock you down' — it pulls the wrong person.
audit.why: Riot on Abscond|Abduct: 'Sylas dashes to a location. Sylas can recast the ability to throw his chains out, pulling himself to an enemy he hits.' The recast drags SYLAS to you, it does not drag you to him. That changes the read completely: after you have spent the taunt on his first dash he can chain himself straight back onto you, so the window you need is both halves spent, not just the dash. Also Kingslayer is itself a dash ('Sylas lunges at an enemy'), on 12/10.5/9/7.5/6s — by rank 5 it is a six-second re-entry, which the page treats as a pure heal.
audit.corrected: Abduct pulls Sylas in, not you. Punch only once both halves of the E are spent, and treat Kingslayer as a second short dash as well as a heal.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names the E with no numbers and never mentions Hijack.
audit.why: Abscond|Abduct 13/12/11/10/9s at 400, Kingslayer 12/10.5/9/7.5/6s at 400, Chain Lash 10/9/8/7/6s at 775, Hijack 80/55/30s at 950, against Justice Punch 11/10/9/8/7s and Hero's Entrance 180/160/140s.
audit.corrected: Cooldown block rebuilt around the two-part E and Hijack.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0] and breakdown.early both say 'your passive shield already blanks his chip'.
audit.why: Galio's passive is Colossal Smash — an empowered basic attack. There is no passive shield, and against a champion who wins by grinding chip damage the false reassurance is exactly the wrong instinct.
audit.corrected: Both lines corrected to describe the passive as offence.

edits.before: Sylas owns the opening levels — his Q chain-lash out-ranges your Colossal Smash poke and his Kingslayer W refunds any trade, while you have no engage until Justice Punch comes up, so concede early CS and last-hit with the tip of Winds of War. By Level 3 you can flip a single window: when he dashes in with E, channel Shield of Durand and release the taunt as he commits, then Justice Punch him so his Kingslayer trade lands into your magic-amplified damage reduction. Respect his E though — it is a dash plus a return chain-pull stun, so if you blow your taunt on the first dash he can still pull you, and you've wasted your only answer.
edits.after: Sylas owns the opening levels — Chain Lash out-ranges your poke and Kingslayer refunds any trade while healing him, and you have no engage until Justice Punch, so concede early CS and last-hit with the tip of Winds of War. By Level 3 you can flip one window: when he dashes in with Abscond, charge Shield of Durand and release the taunt as he commits, then Justice Punch him so the Kingslayer trade lands into your magic-amplified reduction. Know what the recast does, though — Abduct throws his chains out and pulls HIM to you, so he can re-enter after you have spent the taunt.

edits.before: Through 4-5 you trade fine if you only commit when his E is on cooldown, but Level 6 is the knife's edge. Hero's Entrance knocks up and taunts him out of his combo if you land it clean — but Sylas's R is Hijack, which STEALS your ultimate, so a flagged dive can hand him your own global knockup-taunt. Treat your R as a roam tool here: shove with Winds of War and drop into a side lane rather than offering him a free ult to copy. If you must fight at 6, bait his E stun and Kingslayer out first, then engage on his cooldowns.
edits.after: Through 4-5 you trade fine if you only commit when his E is on cooldown, but Level 6 is the knife's edge. Hero's Entrance knocks up and taunts him out of his combo — but Hijack STEALS your ultimate, and it is 80 seconds at rank 1 falling to 30, against your 180. That trade is never in your favour. Treat your R as a roam tool: shove with Winds of War and drop into a side lane rather than handing him a global to copy. If you must fight at 6, bait Abscond and Kingslayer out first.

edits.before: This is where Sylas reclaims the lane. His first AP item turns the Q chain-lash and Kingslayer heal into sustained DPS that grinds through Shield of Durand's mitigation, and by full Riftmaker he simply heals through your damage in any extended fight. The even-AP scaling favours him, and his Hijack makes every teamfight a coinflip when he copies a high-value enemy R. Stop trying to win the duel — your win condition is using Hero's Entrance to be everywhere your enemy isn't, snowballing other lanes so the even 1v1 stops mattering.
edits.after: This is where Sylas reclaims the lane. His first AP item turns Chain Lash and the Kingslayer heal into sustained DPS that grinds through Shield of Durand's mitigation, and by full Riftmaker he heals through your damage in any extended fight — Grievous Wounds is not optional. Hijack is down to 30 seconds by then, so he copies an ultimate almost every fight. Stop trying to win the duel: your win condition is Hero's Entrance being everywhere the enemy isn't, until the even 1v1 stops mattering.

notes: The E's pull direction was backwards on the page — it said Sylas would 'chain-pull stun to lock you down', but Riot's text is 'Sylas can recast the ability to throw his chains out, pulling himself to an enemy he hits'. The recast moves Sylas, not Galio, and that is what makes the taunt-timing rule 'wait for both halves' rather than 'wait for the dash'. I deliberately did NOT write that Abduct stuns: Riot's Data Dragon description does not mention a stun and the kit carries no hardCC flag on that slot, so per the empty-needsResearch rule that is unknown rather than confirmed — I described only the movement, which is stated. UNVERIFIED for the same reason: whether Abduct's arrival interrupts a Shield of Durand charge, and whether a taunted Sylas can still recast. Also worth a look site-wide: Kingslayer is described everywhere as a heal, but Riot calls it a lunge, so it is a second short gap-closer on a cooldown that reaches 6 seconds — a Galio who counts only the E will get re-engaged.
